history.name: Editing the ledger by hand
history.description: The corpus is JSON in the repository, one small file per feature, and its prose is yours to rewrite. You open the file and reword a name, a description, a dev note or the text of a change bullet, add the sentence a coding agent had no way of knowing, or cut a detail the client is better off not reading. Nothing is recorded against a release and nothing is marked as changed, because the product did not move, so the improved wording reads as though it had always been there, including in any earlier edition you reprint. The command ledger status then checks every file, so a description that went missing comes back as a message rather than as a broken build. A change to what the product does goes through ledger add, update or remove, which place it on the right release and refuse a change that never says why it happened.
history.dev_notes: There is no command, deliberately: `ledger reword`, `ledger rename` and `ledger subcategory reword` were removed, and src/cli.mjs RETIRED points each one at the file to edit. Validation on load is what makes hand-editing safe — src/model/feature.mjs Feature#validate runs for every file the store opens, so `ledger status` is the check. `ledger categories rename` stays a command because an area's name is repeated on every feature filed under it.
